data.gender_notes: Amit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Amit is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘amara’ meaning ‘immortal’. This name is associated with the God of Death, Yama, and represents the idea of endless life or immortality. The name is also used as a given name for both boys and girls. The name Amit carries the meaning “Immeasurable, endless” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amit usually hope their child will grow to embody immeasurable, endless and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amit total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Amit, being of Sanskrit origin, holds great significance in Hindu culture. It is often associated with the idea of eternal life or immortality, making the name highly valued and revered within the Hindu community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name Amit symbolizes the ultimate quest for immortality, both in this physical world and in the afterlife. It is believed that those named Amit are granted divine blessings of longevity and eternal happiness. Additionally, the name holds a strong spiritual connection to Yama, the God of Death, whose blessings ensure that the individual's journey through life is peaceful and fulfilling.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amit, meaning limitless or infinite, symbolizes the boundless nature of the soul, transcending all worldly limitations and desires. It is a reminder to strive for spiritual growth and self-realization, beyond the confines of the material world.

vedic_reference.note: The name Amit is derived from the Sanskrit word अमीत (amīt), which means boundless or immeasurable. It is also the name of the god of infinite space, Amitabha, in Buddhist and Jain traditions.

historical_references.reference: Amitasura, a demon king in Hindu mythology, is mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata as one of the asuras (demons) who threatened the gods. He was vanquished by the god Indra using the Vajra, a divine thunderbolt.

Amitabha, a bodhisattva and a central figure in Mahayana Buddhism, is believed to have lived during the time of the historical Buddha. According to legend, Amitabha made a vow to attain enlightenment for the sole purpose of helping others reach enlightenment.
